language_wrapper: In a number system experiment, a positive integer n is called b-augmented if, when expressed in base b with exactly three digits (i.e., its base-b representation has a nonzero leading digit and length three), the sum of those three digits equals sqrt(n) plus {offset}, and n is divisible by {prime}. For b >= {min_b}, let S(b) denote the number of b-augmented integers. Find the least integer b >= {min_b} for which S(b) exceeds {threshold}.
hardness_rationale: This family generalizes the seed by moving from two digits to three digits, introducing an integer offset in the sqrt relation, and imposing an additional divisibility constraint. Solving requires reducing a three-variable base-b Diophantine condition to a quadratic in the digit sum, analyzing an odd-square discriminant, and counting valid triples under modular and range constraints. The extra parameters create edge cases and stricter feasibility conditions, making the minimal-b search more intricate than the seed.
notes: The verifier uses a discriminant-based reduction to avoid an O(b^3) search, keeping performance reasonable for large b while still enforcing the intended structure. The generator retries with varied parameters and falls back to a systematic sweep to ensure a valid instance.
source_question: Let $b \geq 2$ be an integer. Call a positive integer $n$ $b\textit{-eautiful}$ if it has exactly two digits when expressed in base $b$ , and these two digits sum to $\sqrt{n}$ . For example, $81$ is $13$ -eautiful because $81=\underline{6}$ $\underline{3}_{13}$ and $6+3=\sqrt{81}$ . Find the least integer $b\geq 2$ for which there are more than ten $b$ -eautiful integers.
